transport: RS-485 · Modbus RTU · 115200 default baud (vendor manual, DuoRacer V2.5: "Com. baud rate 115200 (default)", settable only via PC software) · default slave ID NOT stated anywhere. Connector is a 3.81 mm 4-pin plug (CC-RS485-RS485-3.81-4P-150 cable supplied), NOT RJ45. On DR1106/2106/3106N the AES port outputs 12 V/200 mA and shares the 5 VDC/200 mA budget with the RS485 port.

There is positive reason to EXPECT a fork rather than assume reuse: the DuoRacer charges a second, separate start battery (BATT2, lead-acid only, max 1 A trickle) and drives an AES refrigerator signal. Neither has any register in the 0x3100/0x3200/0x3300 map, so at minimum the map is extended, and EPEver's habit — demo
Different connector (3.81 mm 4-pin) from the Tracer/XTRA RJ45, which is a weak but real signal of a separately developed comms design.

This one matters more than its evidence suggests, because it is one of only five EPEver controllers a Quebec buyer can actually get from The Cabin Depot. Worth an email to EPEver support asking for the DuoRacer communication protocol document; that is a cheaper path than a bench sweep.

epever.com/download/duoracer-series-resources/ exists but its file list is loaded by JavaScript and could not be retrieved here. A browser session may well find the protocol document there — check before assuming none exists.
unmappedReports: BATT2 — the vehicle start battery. Whatever registers the DuoRacer uses for its second battery's voltage, current and charging state have no counterpart in any EPEver map read in this sweep, and the contract has no way to say WHICH battery a battery-voltage belongs to on a single device. A dual-battery controller is a device reporting two banks through a one-bank vocabulary. This is a contract finding independent of whether the register map is ever found., AES control signal state — the DuoRacer switches a car refrigerator on surplus solar. That is a switch output and a refrigerator interaction with no MetricKind and no CommandKind, on a device the local retailer actually stocks.
